# Implementation Plan: Fretboard Renderer Library

**Branch**: `001-fretboard-renderer` | **Date**: 2025-05-05 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-fretboard-renderer/spec.md`

**Note**: This file generated by following speckit-plan workflow.

---

## Summary

Build a lightweight JavaScript library that renders a guitar fretboard (neck) as SVG with configurable frets (4-16), strings (4-8, default 6), horizontal/vertical orientation, and visual string thickness. Fret number markers appear at standard inlay positions (3, 5, 7, 9, 12). The library exposes position querying APIs to support future interactivity (adding custom markers).

Technical approach: Pure TypeScript library targeting browser environments, outputting SVG elements. No external dependencies for core rendering. Coordinate system maps fret/string indices to pixel positions.

---

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 4.9+
**Primary Dependencies**: N/A (zero external dependencies for core library)
**Storage**: N/A (no persistence required)
**Testing**: Jest with jsdom
**Target Platform**: Browser (last 2 versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
**Project Type**: library
**Performance Goals**: Render complete fretboard < 50ms; bundle size < 10KB minified
**Constraints**: Must not mutate input configuration; SVG output must be valid and render correctly
**Scale/Scope**: Single library supporting 4-16 frets, 4-8 strings; no backend/DB

## Phase 0: Research ✅ COMPLETE

### Resolved Decisions

| ID | Decision | Rationale |
|----|----------|-----------|
| R-001 | TypeScript 4.9+ | Strong typing, better DX, industry standard |
| R-002 | Jest with jsdom | Mature, DOM testing support, good TS integration |
| R-003 | Uniform string thickness | Simpler v1 implementation |
| R-004 | Black on transparent | Maximum compatibility, flexible embedding |
| R-005 | Exclude nut from v1 | Out of scope per spec |
| R-006 | Exclude left-handed from v1 | Out of scope per spec |
| R-007 | Exclude note names from v1 | Out of scope per spec |
